answer: Each identity earns weight only by completing a registered expedition: its controller must walk a multi-day route, checking in at waypoints for a ranger countersignature. The route must wander where no desk-bound operator can fake it, from a glacier crossing to an island ferry checkpoint, timestamped to prove one person walked it. One expedition backs one identity; a reused log or impossible travel time voids both. A farm needs one walker, paying travel, lodging and days of time, per fake, and one walker cannot finish two at once, so fakes scale in bodies, fares and days, not accounts.
